title: Building Sprite Studio MCP for Argon.. video with notes, please give feedback.
author: Lumpy_Conference6640
selftext:
Seems like we’re heading toward a procedural “system of systems” approach to game design. I’ve been tinkering with pretty much every format of game design, and what frustrates me is the stigma around AI-assisted and reverse-engineered games. I honestly think we’re watching a grassroots wave of new game devs show up thanks to AI. And before you can build the next generation of games, you have to understand the last one.

So I’ve been digging into early-90s point-and-click adventures. They’re super easy to click through, and you can iterate on a whole game in an hour, which is what makes them so powerful. To push that further, I’m building tools (and tools for AI to use) that speed up iteration without relying on third-party systems, so compatibility stays as broad as possible.

It’s built on an open-source C++ engine, and I’ll be open-sourcing mine too, but I want it as polished as I can get it first.

**What’s working now:**

* Full animator
* Local ComfyUI/Stable Diffusion integration
* Folder-based project system

**Coming once my credits roll over:**

* Flow/Nano Banana 2 MCP for unlimited cloud generations
* LoRA support for design consistency
* Adaptive UI/UX
* Built-in local background remover

Would love to hear what features you’d want in something like this, or any recommendations. Thanks!
